raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`topkGating` (`csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu`) gives each row to one full warp when the row is wide enough (512 experts, 256 experts with 16-bit logits, 128-512 experts with fp32 logits). For each of the k selections it runs a 5-stage shuffle butterfly with 3 dependent shuffles per stage, then lane 0 stores the selection and later re-reads the weights to scale them.

For those rows, without a correction bias, this PR selects each expert with two `redux.sync` reductions (`__reduce_max_sync` on the score key, then `__reduce_min_sync` on the expert among the lanes that hold the max), keeps selection i in the registers of lane i, rescans only in the winning lane, and writes the row once at the end. The output is bitwise equal to `main`: the same experts, the same order, the same lowest-index tie rule and the same weight bits.

The register-resident output path is from @Gin-Sin (#64731, co-author); the SM80+ `redux.sync` selection scope is from this PR. #64731 will be closed in favour of this PR.

## Claims

- **Same output:** bitwise equal to `main` (ids, weights as bits, token-expert indices) in every case run on A100, including tie-heavy, all-equal and NaN/Inf rows.
- **Faster on SM80+:** E 512 top-10 softmax on A100: 0.59-0.68x of `main`'s time at 1-256 tokens, 0.71-0.76x at 1,024-4,096 tokens. On B300 (measured by @Gin-Sin): 1.7-2.7x faster than `main` at every full-warp shape.
- **End to end:** below serving noise. On B300 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, DP4 + EP, MTP 3, with the #64731 output path) throughput changed by at most about 1 %, inside the main-vs-main spread; GSM8K and greedy outputs are unchanged. Against `main`, the kernel saves 2.7-4.7 us per router call on A100 (1-256 tokens) and 2.5-6.9 us on B300 (E 512, 1-464 tokens).
- **No change elsewhere:** biased routing, k > 32, sub-warp rows (for example E 128 with 16-bit logits), ROCm and pre-SM80 GPUs keep the current loop, which is byte-identical to `main`. No new CPU/GPU sync, no new launch, no change to the op schema.

## Validation

**Kernel A/B, one A100-SXM4-40GB (sm_80), 31 Oct 2026.** Four copies of `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` are built side by side as separate `torch.utils.cpp_extension` modules (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13, `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80`): `main` 17550580e9, the first revision of this PR c7f8f96ee8, #64731 7a51d76027, and this PR c752616c1d. Each time is per call under CUDA graph replay (100 calls x 20 replays, minimum of 3 interleaved rounds). E 512, top-10, softmax, renormalize.

| logits | tokens | main | first revision | #64731 | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 1 | 9.99 us | 7.69 us | 6.48 us | **5.31 us** |
| fp32 | 8 | 8.35 us | 6.36 us | 5.77 us | **5.34 us** |
| fp32 | 64 | 8.69 us | 6.71 us | 5.69 us | **5.37 us** |
| fp32 | 256 | 9.01 us | 7.12 us | 5.85 us | **5.38 us** |
| fp32 | 1,024 | 11.84 us | 10.90 us | 9.17 us | **8.71 us** |
| fp32 | 4,096 | 26.54 us | 25.54 us | 21.60 us | **20.25 us** |
| bf16 | 1 | 7.79 us | 5.85 us | 5.45 us | **5.02 us** |
| bf16 | 8 | 8.56 us | 6.62 us | 5.76 us | **5.33 us** |
| bf16 | 64 | 8.67 us | 6.73 us | 5.72 us | **5.24 us** |
| bf16 | 256 | 9.00 us | 7.05 us | 5.76 us | **5.38 us** |
| bf16 | 1,024 | 11.74 us | 10.76 us | 9.03 us | **8.35 us** |
| bf16 | 4,096 | 26.35 us | 25.37 us | 21.47 us | **19.98 us** |

Bitwise checks against `main` on the same A100: every timed case above, plus 36 tie-heavy cases (fp32 / bf16 / fp16 x tokens 1 / 7 / 64 / 333 x few distinct values / all-equal rows / wide randn): 0 mismatches for all three changed copies. 

**B300 (sm_100), measured by @Gin-Sin on this head c752616c1d** ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62912#issuecomment-6541421469)): CUDA 13.1, FlashInfer CUPTI timing with CUDA graph and cold L2, median of 3 rotated rounds; bitwise equal to `main` in 336/336 case-runs.

| logits | E / top-k | tokens | main | #64731 | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 1 | 6.50 us | 4.00 us | **3.78 us** |
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 64 | 8.86 us | 3.97 us | **3.74 us** |
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 464 | 11.04 us | 4.32 us | **4.10 us** |
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 8,192 | 32.96 us | 19.90 us | **18.62 us** |
| fp32 | 256 / 8 | 64 | 7.78 us | 3.36 us | **3.17 us** |
| bf16 | 128 / 8 (sub-warp, unchanged path) | 64 | 6.24 us | 6.24 us | 6.24 us |

End-to-end serving and GSM8K on B300 with the #64731 output path are in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62912#issuecomment-6536962624): no difference beyond run-to-run noise at concurrency 16/64, about +1 % at 464 (at the edge of noise); GSM8K 0.967/0.969 (main) vs 0.971/0.969; greedy outputs identical on 200/200 prompts.

## Details

**Why it is exact.** Without a bias the choice score is the output score. After softmax or sigmoid and the existing NaN/Inf clamp every score is >= +0, so the unsigned order of the float bits is the float order. Each lane offers `key = score bits + 1` for its best unselected slot (a selected slot has key 0). The first `redux.sync` finds the maximum key; the second finds the minimum expert among lanes that hold it, which is the lowest expert index, the same tie rule as the butterfly. Only the owner lane clears its slot and rescans. Lane i keeps selection i; lanes 0..k-1 write once at the end, with the same fp32 renormalization sum order and the same scale as `main`.

**Scope.** `topkGating` rows with `THREADS_PER_ROW == WARP_SIZE`, no bias, k <= 32, `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800`, not ROCm; the launcher picks a separate `FULL_WARP_SELECT` instantiation, so the existing loop's code generation does not change. Rows beyond `num_rows` return per warp before the selection, so all 32 lanes reach each `redux.sync`. TensorRT-LLM uses `redux.sync` for this selection on SM100+.

**Tests.** `test_topk_without_bias_matches_zero_bias` (from #64731, extended) compares a launch without a bias against a launch with an all-zero bias, which keeps the old loop, bit for bit: E 128/352/384/512/576, k 1/10/32, bf16/fp16/fp32, softmax/sigmoid, renormalize on/off, `is_padding` rows, `routed_scaling_factor`, tie-heavy rows with NaN/+Inf, and the tie order against a stable sort (720 cases). It has not run in a full vLLM build on our side; CI will run it. The benchmark gains a `--dtype` option for fp32 router logits.

**CI.** There is no sm_80 runner. The A100 data come from our cluster.

**Related.** #64731 (Gin-Sin, same selection; its output path is folded in here). #59737 (PDL for this kernel, SM90+ only) does not overlap. #57823 (padded row strides) touches the same file.

- Each lane keeps its selection in registers, and the row is written once at the end; only the winning lane rescans.
- #62912 stores to global memory every round and reads the weights back.

| 464 | main 0-3, kernel 4-7 | 17,203 / 16,786 | 17,103 / 17,331 | +1.3% | −1.1% | 2.39-2.47 per run, all arms |
| 464 | swapped | 17,100 / 17,071 | 17,184 / 17,229 | +0.7% | −0.2% | |

| 464 | noise: main vs main | 16,868 / 17,221 | 16,703 / 17,111 | −0.8% | −1.5% | |

**Verdict:**

**Kernel A/B, one A100-SXM4-40GB (sm_80), 31 Oct 2026.** Four copies of `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` are built side by side as separate `torch.utils.cpp_extension` modules (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13, `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80`): `main` 17550580e9, the first revision of this PR c7f8f96ee8, #64731 7a51d76027, and this PR c752616c1d. Each time is per call under CUDA graph replay (100 calls x 20 replays, minimum of 3 interleaved rounds). E 512, top-10, softmax, renormalize.

## Details

**Why it is exact.** Without a bias the choice score is the output score. After softmax or sigmoid and the existing NaN/Inf clamp every score is >= +0, so the unsigned order of the float bits is the float order. Each lane offers `key = score bits + 1` for its best unselected slot (a selected slot has key 0). The first `redux.sync` finds the maximum key; the second finds the minimum expert among lanes that hold it, which is the lowest expert index, the same tie rule as the butterfly. Only the owner lane clears its slot and rescans. Lane i keeps selection i; lanes 0..k-1 write once at the end, with the same fp32 renormalization sum order and the same scale as `main`.

**Scope.** `topkGating` rows with `THREADS_PER_ROW == WARP_SIZE`, no bias, k <= 32, `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800`, not ROCm; the launcher picks a separate `FULL_WARP_SELECT` instantiation, so the existing loop's code generation does not change. Rows beyond `num_rows` return per warp before the selection, so all 32 lanes reach each `redux.sync`. TensorRT-LLM uses `redux.sync` for this selection on SM100+.

**Tests.** `test_topk_without_bias_matches_zero_bias` (from #64731, extended) compares a launch without a bias against a launch with an all-zero bias, which keeps the old loop, bit for bit: E 128/352/384/512/576, k 1/10/32, bf16/fp16/fp32, softmax/sigmoid, renormalize on/off, `is_padding` rows, `routed_scaling_factor`, tie-heavy rows with NaN/+Inf, and the tie order against a stable sort (720 cases). It has not run in a full vLLM build on our side; CI will run it. The benchmark gains a `--dtype` option for fp32 router logits.

**CI.** There is no sm_80 runner. The A100 data come from our cluster.

**Related.** #64731 (Gin-Sin, same selection; its output path is folded in here). #59737 (PDL for this kernel, SM90+ only) does not overlap. #57823 (padded row strides) touches the same file.

 import pytest
 import torch
 
+import vllm._custom_ops as ops
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.fused_topk_bias_router import (
     fused_topk_bias,
 )
@@ -275,3 +276,98 @@ def test_fused_topk_bias_nan_inf_clamp(
             f"Row {row} has non-finite weights {topk_weights[row].tolist()} "
             f"(bad_value={bad_value}, scoring_func={scoring_func})"
         )
+
+
+def _tie_heavy_logits(
+    num_tokens: int, num_experts: int, dtype: torch.dtype
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Small integer logits, so most scores tie exactly with other experts.
+
+    Row 0 is constant (every expert ties). With enough rows, row 1 is NaN and
+    row 2 is +Inf, so the NaN/Inf clamp or a constant sigmoid makes every
+    score tie.
+    """
+    logits = torch.randint(-2, 3, (num_tokens, num_experts), device="cuda").to(dtype)
+    logits[0] = 1.0
+    if num_tokens > 2:
+        logits[1] = float("nan")
+        logits[2] = float("inf")
+    return logits
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda_alike(),
+    reason="This test is skipped on non-CUDA platform.",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 2047])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_experts", [128, 352, 384, 512, 576])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topk", [1, 10, 32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("renormalize", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scoring_func", ["softmax", "sigmoid"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.half, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ties", [False, True])
+def test_topk_without_bias_matches_zero_bias(
+    num_tokens: int,
+    num_experts: int,
+    topk: int,
+    renormalize: bool,
+    scoring_func: str,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    ties: bool,
+):
+    """Without a correction bias, rows that one full warp owns select with
+    redux.sync on SM80+. An all-zero bias gives the same choice scores but
+    keeps the original selection loop, so both launches must match bit for
+    bit: weights, expert ids and token_expert_indices, including the
+    lowest-index tie rule, NaN/Inf rows, padding rows and the scaling.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    if ties:
+        gating_output = _tie_heavy_logits(num_tokens, num_experts, dtype)
+    else:
+        gating_output = torch.randn(
+            (num_tokens, num_experts), dtype=dtype, device="cuda"
+        )
+    is_padding = torch.arange(num_tokens, device="cuda") % 5 == 4
+    zero_bias = torch.zeros(num_experts, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    extra_args = {"routed_scaling_factor": 2.5} if scoring_func == "sigmoid" else {}
+    topk_func = ops.topk_softmax if scoring_func == "softmax" else ops.topk_sigmoid
+
+    outputs = []
+    for bias in (None, zero_bias):
+        topk_weights = torch.empty(
+            (num_tokens, topk), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda"
+        )
+        topk_ids = torch.empty((num_tokens, topk), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        token_expert_indices = torch.empty_like(topk_ids)
+        topk_func(
+            topk_weights,
+            topk_ids,
+            token_expert_indices,
+            gating_output,
+            renormalize=renormalize,
+            e_score_correction_bias=bias,
+            is_padding=is_padding,
+            **extra_args,
+        )
+        outputs.append((topk_weights.view(torch.int32), topk_ids, token_expert_indices))
+
+    for out, ref in zip(*outputs):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+    if ties:
+        # Equal logits give equal scores, so a stable sort fixes the tie order.
+        scores = (
+            torch.softmax(gating_output.float(), dim=-1)
+            if scoring_func == "softmax"
+            else torch.sigmoid(gating_output.float())
+        )
+        scores = torch.nan_to_num(scores, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0)
+        expected_ids = torch.sort(scores, dim=-1, descending=True, stable=True)[1]
+        topk_ids = outputs[0][1]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            topk_ids[~is_padding],
+            expected_ids[~is_padding, :topk].to(torch.int32),
+            atol=0,
+            rtol=0,
+        )

Hi @kimseunghyun-kr, thanks for this PR. I was working on the same `topkGating` full-warp path and ended up with a very similar `redux.sync` selection. I just opened #64731 as a draft to share the code and numbers, and I'd like to converge with you rather than compete.

The difference is the output path:
- Each lane keeps its selection in registers, and the row is written once at the end; only the winning lane rescans.
- #62912 stores to global memory every round and reads the weights back.

On B300 (E=512, top-10, fp32 softmax), all three bitwise equal to main in 11,520 cases:

| Tokens | main | #62912 | #64731 |

| 1 | 5.33 µs | 3.97 µs | 3.05 µs |

| 128 | 8.88 µs | 7.59 µs | 3.10 µs |
| 4096 | 19.96 µs | 19.69 µs | 15.71 µs |

An ablation (my selection with your per-round store) runs at your PR's speed, so the gap comes from the write path.
